shorts.title: A Walrus Mouth Pulls Nearly a Vacuum, With Its Tongue
shorts.outro: The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: A captive walrus sucking on a pressure sensor pulled almost 88 kilopascals below normal air pressure, close to a vacuum, and what that mouth did to Doug's open palm is in the full episode linked below.

cliffhanger_original.hook: A walrus eats a clam without ever opening it.
cliffhanger_original.outro: Then Doug held out a clam to that mouth, on his open palm. What came back is in the full video below.
cliffhanger_original.end_card: WHAT CAME BACK IN DOUG'S HAND?

shorts.title: A Walrus Mother Sank a Russian Navy Boat
shorts.outro: The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: In 2019 a walrus protecting her calf sank a Northern Fleet landing boat at Franz Josef Land, and what she did to Doug's dinghy is in the full episode linked below.

cliffhanger_original.outro: Doug then rowed a tiny dinghy past a mother with a calf on her back, and waved. Full video below.
cliffhanger_original.end_card: WHAT DID SHE DO TO DOUG'S DINGHY?

shorts.title: 35,000 Walruses Crowded Onto One Alaska Beach
shorts.description: In September 2014 about 35,000 walruses hauled out near Point Lay, Alaska, roughly a hundred for every person in town, and what happens when they all run for the sea is in the full episode linked below.

cliffhanger_original.outro: And when one low plane spooks all thirty-five thousand at once, Doug is standing between them and the sea. It's linked below.

shorts.hook: Thirty-five thousand walruses once hauled out near Point Lay, Alaska.
